findings.title: Bulk of business-logic tests run only against the SQLAlchemy create_all schema, not the hand-maintained Alembic migration
findings.why_it_matters: conftest.py's `engine` fixture (used by every test_jobs.py/test_tailor.py/test_resume.py/test_recommendations.py/test_health.py test — the overwhelming majority of the 113 tests) builds the schema via `SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine)`, generated directly from the SQLModel class definitions. Only test_models.py's dedicated `migrated_engine` fixture actually runs `alembic upgrade head` against the hand-written 0001_initial_schema.py revision, and it is exercised by only 3 tests that check table-name presence, one cascade, and the partial unique index — not column-level parity (nullability, types, defaults, FK ondelete actions) with models.py. The migration file's own docstring admits the risk: 'Hand-written rather than autogenerated ... Keep it in sync with app/models.py' — a manual invariant with no automated check beyond table-name inspection. If a future migration (or even this one, undetected) diverges from a model — e.g. a column that's nullable in the migration but NOT NULL in the model, or a FK ondelete action that differs — the 100+ business-logic tests exercising jobs/tailor/resume/recommendations behavior would still pass green against the create_all schema while the real production DB (built by `alembic upgrade head`, per backend/README.md's documented startup) behaves differently. This is exactly the kind of regression that slips through: schema drift invisible to CI because the test suite's dominant fixture doesn't use the same schema-construction path as production.
evidence: backend/tests/conftest.py:20-23 — `create_all` used for the shared `engine`/`client` fixtures with a comment stating the real migration path is 'exercised in test_models.py'

backend/tests/test_models.py:243-297 — `migrated_engine` fixture + only test_migration_creates_all_model_tables (table names only), test_migrated_db_round_trips_and_cascades, and test_migrated_db_enforces_partial_source_ref_index use it
backend/alembic/versions/0001_initial_schema.py:3-5 — 'Hand-written rather than autogenerated ... Keep it in sync with app/models.py' (an unenforced manual invariant)

findings.title: Cross-job 404 branch tested only for comments, not contacts or links (identical code, untested duplicate branches)
findings.why_it_matters: `delete_contact` and `delete_link` in jobs.py each have the same 'wrong parent job' 404 check (`contact.job_id != job_id` / `link.job_id != job_id`) as `delete_comment`, but only `test_deleting_sub_resource_from_wrong_job_returns_404` (comments) exercises this branch. A future refactor that accidentally drops or inverts the job_id check on contacts/links (e.g. during a DRY-up of the three near-identical delete handlers) would not be caught by any test.
evidence: backend/app/routers/jobs.py:288-300 (delete_comment), :327-339 (delete_contact), :366-377 (delete_link) — three copies of the same ownership-check branch
backend/tests/test_jobs.py:388-397 — test_deleting_sub_resource_from_wrong_job_returns_404 only creates comments on job_a/job_b, never contacts or links
findings.suggested_fix: Parametrize test_deleting_sub_resource_from_wrong_job_returns_404 (or add two sibling tests) to also create a contact and a link on job_a and assert DELETE through job_b's URL returns 404 for each, mirroring the comment case.

residual_risks: The plan's U2 verification promise — 'alembic upgrade head builds the schema from empty *and* upgrades a populated fixture (batch-mode rebuild exercised)' — is only half-true today: since there is a single revision (0001_initial_schema.py, `create_table` only), there is no ALTER/table-rebuild for batch mode to actually perform, so `render_as_batch=True` in alembic/env.py is configured but never exercised by any test. This will only become a real test until a second migration lands; worth tracking so the first schema-changing migration is required to add a batch-mode-rebuild-against-populated-DB test alongside it.

The plan states 'the SQLite write lock is never held across a Claude or JSearch call' as a tested invariant for U5/U6. What's actually tested is transactional atomicity (no partial rows after a failure) and code-level ordering (network calls before the transaction opens) — not genuine concurrent-lock contention under a real second writer/reader. This is a reasonable trade-off given SQLite/TestClient's single-threaded test execution, but the 'reader never blocks' guarantee itself is unverified by any test in this diff.
testing_gaps: Column/constraint-level parity between the hand-written Alembic migration and the SQLModel table definitions has no automated check beyond table-name presence — a schema drift here would pass the full suite (see finding above).
